business_scope.primary_industry_name: C-Suite Executive Search and Specialist Tech Headhunting

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: A Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) is constituted under the Civil Code of Québec, including articles 2186 and 2236–2249. Registration and disclosure are governed by the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, including its registration requirements. This is partnership formation, not incorporation of a corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), administered by the Ministère de l’Emploi et de la Solidarité sociale
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d’immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed in the Québec Enterprise Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or paid-up-capital escrow is prescribed for a Quebec limited partnership. The partnership agreement should specify each partner’s contribution. The general partner manages the partnership; limited partners should not take part in its administration toward third parties, subject to the Civil Code rules governing their liability.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The general partner, acting for the limited partnership, resolves that the partnership agreement and the initial subscriptions and contributions of the partners are approved, subject to execution of the agreement and applicable law. The partnership’s registered office is adopted at [Quebec address], and the general partner is authorized to file or update the required declaration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. [Name] is appointed authorized representative for registry filings and [Name] is appointed finance and compliance officer. The authorized representative may open partnership bank accounts, obtain tax accounts, and execute documents necessary to implement these resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners; Quebec notary or lawyer where professional drafting or authentication is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the partnership name, identify the general and limited partners, determine contributions, profit allocations, management authority, transfer restrictions, and dissolution terms. Execute a written partnership agreement before commencing business. Quebec law does not generally require notarization of the agreement; obtain notarization or certified copies when required by a bank, foreign authority, or transaction counterparty.
required_dossiers: Executed limited partnership agreement
Identity and address details for each partner and the general partner
Evidence of partner authority, if a partner is an entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise incomplete or inconsistent terms, obtain missing authority evidence, and re-execute before filing or relying on the agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec through its online services or the applicable government filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration with the partnership’s name, Quebec domicile, activity, general partner, required partner and administrator particulars, and authorized representative information. Pay the applicable REQ fee. File within the statutory period applicable to the partnership; confirm the current deadline and fee in the REQ portal. The stated USD fee is an approximate conversion of a Quebec-dollar filing fee and is not the amount payable.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration
Partnership name and Quebec address
Partner and general partner particulars
Entity documents and proof of authority for any entity partner
Payment of the current REQ filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the REQ channel by the stated deadline, correct rejected fields or name conflicts, provide requested supporting documents, and resubmit. Verify the registration number and filed information in the Québec Enterprise Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online; Revenu Québec online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a CRA business number and register for applicable program accounts, including GST/HST, payroll deductions, and import/export only where relevant. Register with Revenu Québec for applicable QST and source-deduction accounts. Determine registration obligations based on revenue, activities, and hiring; do not assume that partnership registration alone creates all tax accounts.
required_dossiers: REQ registration number
Partnership agreement
General partner and authorized representative information
Business activity, address, and expected commencement date
Payroll and revenue estimates, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct account information through the relevant tax authority, submit missing ownership or identity documents, and obtain written confirmation of effective dates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Quebec personnel placement agency permit where the service is regulated
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission des normes, de l’équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before providing services that fall within Quebec’s regulated personnel placement agency activities, apply for the required agency permit through CNESST and satisfy applicable fee, security, and compliance conditions. Confirm in writing with CNESST whether the planned direct-hire executive search model is within the statutory definition; do not treat the ISIC code alone as determinative. Do not conduct covered activities before the permit is effective.
required_dossiers: REQ registration and partnership details
General partner and controlling-person identity information
Business address and description of recruitment activities
CNESST application, required fee, and any required financial security
Compliance declarations and supporting documents requested by CNESST
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide clarifications and missing documents within the CNESST deadline, correct deficiencies, and seek administrative review or other available remedies if the application is refused. Suspend covered placement activity until authorization is effective.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish ongoing enterprise-register and governance compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec; partners and general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain required partnership and beneficial ownership information, update changes through the prescribed REQ declaration, and submit annual updating declarations and applicable annual duties on time. Keep the partnership agreement, contribution records, financial records, permit records, and partner decisions at the registered office or another lawful location.
required_dossiers: Current partnership agreement and amendments
Partner contribution and distribution records
Current REQ particulars and beneficial ownership information, as applicable
Annual updating declaration and applicable payment records
CNESST permit and renewal records, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File overdue or corrective declarations promptly, pay applicable charges, and contact the REQ or CNESST to regularize status and address any cancellation, penalty, or enforcement notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission des normes, de l’équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) for a personnel placement agency permit where the proposed recruitment activities are covered by Quebec law; no industrial manufacturing board applies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis d’agence de placement de personnel, if the activities fall within the applicable Quebec statutory definition

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from project-specific environmental assessment for office-based executive search and recruitment activities, absent a separate prescribed project or regulated site activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industry-specific wastewater, VOC, or industrial-waste thresholds ordinarily apply to an office-only search business. Comply with applicable municipal sewer and waste rules, building requirements, and general environmental law if site activities create regulated discharges or wastes.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No sector-specific fire, structural-load, or industrial workplace clearance ordinarily applies to an office-only operation. The premises must satisfy applicable municipal building and fire-safety requirements, and the employer must comply with Quebec occupational health and safety duties. Confirm any occupancy, fire, or accessibility requirements with the municipality and building owner.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online (BRO); Revenu Québec – Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) and Revenu Québec Online Services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing or investing in a Quebec limited partnership must register the partnership with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain a Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ). For federal tax purposes, the partnership obtains a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) through Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1. The general partner (resident or non-resident) applies on behalf of the limited partnership. If the LP makes taxable supplies in excess of CAD 30,000, it must register for GST/HST. Quebec requires separate registration for QST through Revenu Québec. Non-resident general partners may need to provide evidence of Canadian representative status or power of attorney where required. The LP must file annual information returns (T5013), and Quebec requires an equivalent Relevé 15 or annual provincial filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canadian limited partnerships are statutorily classified as flow-through entities for income tax purposes; no check-the-box election exists. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act (notably section 18.4 and related provisions) apply to prevent deduction/non-inclusion mismatches where a foreign jurisdiction treats the entity differently. Partnerships may file joint elections under subsection 97(2) of the Income Tax Act for tax-deferred transfers of property to the partnership and may adopt a non-calendar taxation year under subsection 96(3) with CRA approval. Quebec follows the federal classification for QST and provincial income tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and Quebec Sales Tax (TVQ/QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide taxable supplies for GST/HST; CAD 30,000 for QST in Quebec. Non-residents with no permanent establishment in Canada may have modified registration obligations, but a non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada must generally register once the threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Federal GST/HST does not currently mandate real-time electronic clearance or government-approved digital stamping. Electronic invoices are accepted if they contain prescribed information under section 3 of the Excise Tax Act. Quebec has implemented a mandatory electronic invoicing and e-reporting regime for QST registrants, phased in from 2023 to 2025, requiring B2B invoices to be transmitted through a software provider certified by Revenu Québec. No continuous transaction control (CTC) real-time clearance exists federally or provincially.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI (Excise Tax Act). Services supplied to a non-resident may be zero-rated if the service is performed wholly or mainly outside Canada, or relates directly to exported goods. Executive search and headhunting services provided to non-resident clients may qualify for zero-rating if the recipient is a non-resident and the service is not in connection with real property located in Canada or tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time of supply. The supplier must maintain sufficient documentary evidence of the non-resident status and of the place of performance or benefit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or CERS electronic filing)
Commercial invoice for goods or services
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (for goods)
Proof of export control data (PARS/ACI release documentation)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire confirmation evidencing foreign currency receipt
Retainer agreement / engagement letter identifying non-resident client and jurisdiction
GST/HST zero-rating support documentation (non-resident status evidence, place-of-supply substantiation)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the Excise Tax Act, an exporter that zero-rates without proper substantiation may be assessed GST/HST, interest and penalties. Penalties include a 5% failure-to-remit penalty plus 1% per month (uncapped), gross negligence penalties of 50% of the amount, and a 100% penalty for false statements or omissions. Criminal prosecution is possible for wilful evasion. The CRA can reassess within four years of the date of assessment; longer reassessment periods apply in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. Revenu Québec may apply similar QST clawbacks and penalties, including interest and fines. Retrospective clawbacks may also include denial of input tax credits and recovery of zero-rated refunds previously paid. Executive search and headhunting services are scrutinized for evidence that the service was actually rendered to a non-resident and enjoyed outside Canada; insufficient documentation can lead to domestic supply characterization and full tax recovery.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), with prudential banking supervision exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), anti-money-laundering supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and corporate registry administration by the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ). Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange-control authority analogous to SAFE; FX administration is market-based and governed by the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations; both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible without government approval or repatriation licensing. The Canadian dollar (CAD) is a fully convertible, floating currency. For a Quebec Limited Partnership engaged in executive search, inbound retainer payments from foreign clients and outbound partnership distributions are unrestricted. Repatriation of profits to non-resident limited partners is not subject to exchange control, but the Income Tax Act Part XIII withholding tax applies to specified Canadian-source payments (management fees, interest, royalties, and certain partnership allocations), and non-resident partners carrying on business in Canada through the LP are taxed under section 115 via CRA and Revenu Québec filings. Practical hurdles are limited to tax compliance, CRS/FATCA reporting, and the bank's own anti-money-laundering (AML) due diligence rather than FX licensing. No prior central-bank or OSFI approval is required for foreign direct investment into the LP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no forced repatriation of foreign-currency export proceeds. The CA_LP executive-search enterprise may retain USD, EUR, or GBP denominated retainers indefinitely in foreign-currency operating accounts with Canadian Schedule I banks, or convert to CAD at negotiated market spreads. The only compliance requirements are disclosure-based: FINTRAC reporting by the financial institution for single international electronic fund transfers (EFTs) of CAD 10,000 or more, the LP's T5013 Partnership Information Return allocation of Canadian-source business income to partners, and FATCA/CRS beneficial-ownership reporting for non-resident partners.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (CAD + USD dual-currency structure)
Operational Deposit Account / Escrow-Like Retainer Trust Account (CAD, with USD via Desjardins Business FX desk)
Capital Escrow Account / Business Operating Account (CAD and USD sweeps)
Operating Account / Capital Contribution Account (CAD, USD, and cross-border cash management)
Business Operating Account / Retainer Collection Account (CAD/USD)
Business Deposit Account / USD Payables Account
Operating Account / International FX Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium, slated as a supplementary settlement rail, not a primary treasury repository. Wise Canada Inc. (Wise B2B) is registered as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and is a viable corridor for low-value cross-border retainer disbursements and subcontractor payments (USD, EUR, GBP, SEK, and 40+ currencies). Legal constraints: (i) Wise is not a Schedule I/Schedule II chartered bank and does not provide CDIC deposit insurance; (ii) the LP must maintain its primary capital escrow account and legal corporate account at an OSFI-supervised bank because Quebec retainer-escrow and partnership capital obligations require a regulated financial institution; (iii) Wise's platform may cap high-value transfers and requires a whitelisted counterparty list to satisfy the LP's internal treasury controls; (iv) all Wise-originated or Wise-received transfers of CAD 10,000 or more are subject to FINTRAC EFT reporting, so the LP must preserve underlying engagement documentation; and (v) Wise cannot provide commercial letters of credit, performance guarantees, or credit facilities. Therefore, use Wise B2B exclusively for operational expense disbursements and small sub-retainer payments, while all client retainers, capital injections, and profit distributions flow through the primary chartered-bank accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec limited partnership with a corporate general partner and any non-resident limited partner, most Quebec-headquartered banks mandate a physical identity verification step at a Quebec branch for at least one individual with signing authority, typically the corporate general partner's designated director or officer. Fully remote account opening is generally not available for partnerships with non-resident ownership, even in a Low-Risk Standard AML tier. Acceptable alternatives: (i) notarized signature and passport verification by a Canadian notary, followed by a video interview with the relationship manager; (ii) apostilled corporate and partnership documents from the GP's home jurisdiction; (iii) an in-country banking introduction via a correspondent bank or existing advisory relationship; or (iv) a remote KYC interview with credit-bureau identity verification (via Equifax Canada or TransUnion) where the bank's internal CDD policy permits. Practical recommendation: the corporate general partner should anticipate sending the signing officer to Montreal or Quebec City for a 30-minute onboarding session at National Bank or Desjardins, as this materially accelerates account activation, FX limits, and wire approval thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partnership ownership opacity: LP structure with a corporate general partner plus non-resident limited partners, potentially obscuring ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) REQ certificate of registration (attestation d'immatriculation) with NEQ number; (ii) notarized partnership agreement (acte de société) and, where applicable, a trust declaration; (iii) full UBO schedule listing every partner with 25% or greater interest and all directors of the corporate general partner; (iv) certified corporate registry extracts of the GP from its home jurisdiction; (v) organizational chart certified by the GP's corporate secretary; and (vi) current and historical bank reference letters from the partners' primary financial institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner jurisdiction risk: inbounds from or partner tax residency in FATF-monitored or higher-risk jurisdictions, or transfers from a jurisdiction exhibiting sanctions exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) CRA individual or corporate tax residency certificates and, for Quebec, Revenu Québec residency confirmations; (ii) passport plus proof of physical residence (utility bill, lease, government-issued ID); (iii) source-of-wealth declaration with supporting asset statements, share-sale contracts, employment contracts, or audited group financial statements; (iv) source-of-funds evidence for all capital contributions, with 12-month bank statements from the remitting institution; (v) negative media/sanctions screening reports; and (vi) a written enhanced-due-diligence response letter prepared by the LP's compliance officer or attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Retainer-based fee red flag: the executive-search model receives large placement fees without physical goods, raising suspicion of commission laundering or undisclosed third-party beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Duly executed retainer agreements and client engagement letters naming the CA_LP as the sole service provider; (ii) detailed invoices with unique invoice numbers, placement descriptions, candidate role titles, and fee calculation formulas; (iii) service-delivery evidence (search mandates, candidate shortlists, interview schedules, placement confirmations, and billing approvals by the client); (iv) the LP's fee policy confirming no contingent-fee recruiting activity; (v) Quebec personnel-placement licensing posture: REQ registration plus, if applicable, a permit under the Quebec Act respecting personnel placement agencies (CQLR c. P-16.1) or a written exemption opinion from Quebec counsel for C-suite executive-search-only mandates; and (vi) a no-commingling attestation for any prepaid retainer balances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Fintech rail exposure: use of Wise B2B or similar EMIs for cross-border disbursements may be perceived as unregulated third-party settlement and a control failure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Corporate resolution of the general partner expressly authorizing Wise B2B as a designated disbursement rail and naming the authorized treasury signatories; (ii) treasury policy limiting Wise to per-transaction caps and counterparty whitelisting; (iii) end-to-end reconciliation reports matching each Wise transfer to an underlying client engagement or subcontractor agreement; (iv) FINTRAC MSB verification evidence for the Wise entity; and (v) quarterly A/B clearing-rail audit comparing Wise versus SWIFT MT103 charges to demonstrate prudent treasury management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow-like prepaid retainers: clients may prepay large search retainers, creating trust-account concerns and potential liability for misuse of client funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Escrow or trust agreement governed by Quebec civil law naming the bank or a licensed trust company as depositary, or a clearly segregated retainer-subaccount ledger at the primary Schedule I bank; (ii) written client acknowledgment that prepaid retainers are held in the LP's operating account only for invoiced services; (iii) monthly reconciliation of cash balances against unbilled-retainer obligations; (iv) audited or reviewed financial statements evidencing proper liability classification; and (v) directors' resolution adopting a client-funds protection policy with audit rights.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire protocol for the initial and ongoing capital contributions from non-resident partners: the remitting partner originates an international wire via SWIFT MT103 to the LP's beneficiary account at a Schedule I bank in Quebec. Mandatory fields: (i) beneficiary name must exactly match the REQ-registered partnership name and LP number; (ii) field 70 (Remittance Information) must state CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - CA_LP - [partnership NEQ or REQ registration number]; (iii) beneficiary bank account must be the dedicated Capital Escrow Account with the account title General Partner c/o [LP name]; and (iv) the remitter must provide to its bank the LP's registered address in Quebec and the GP's full identification. For banks requiring a purpose or reason code, use EQUITY CAPITAL / PARTNERSHIP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION rather than trade-related codes. Documentary packet to be provided to the receiving branch: executed capital-contribution resolution, updated partner ledger, source-of-funds statements for amounts exceeding CAD 10,000, and a signed indemnity confirming no Part XIII withholding applies to capital contributions. After credit, the LP must record the receipt in its capital schedule and reflect the allocation in the annual T5013 partnership return. Foreign currencies are accepted only in USD, EUR, or GBP; CAD conversion is executed at the bank's commercial rate with an FX conversion invoice for FATCA/CRS transparency.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Given the ISIC 7830 executive-search scope, outbound clearing rails are optimized for services, retainer refunds, and subcontractor fees rather than merchandise trade. Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 for international payments to non-resident subcontractor headhunters, partner agencies, and independent consultants, using SWIFT field 70 with the underlying invoice and placement-reference number to support TRC (travel rules compliance). Domestic CAD and USD payments between Canadian participants use the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or the bank's EFT batch, with same-day settlement for wire-class disbursements above CAD 25,000. Secondary rail: Wise B2B for low-value (under CAD 15,000) disbursements in non-USD corridors such as EUR, GBP, SEK, and INR, with a monthly reconciliation feed feeding the partnership's treasury ledger. Commercial letters of credit are not applicable to headhunting services because no physical goods or title documents exist; however, a standby letter of credit (SBLC) may be requested by blue-chip client programs as a performance guarantee and can be issued against the LP's operating-balance collateral at National Bank or RBC. Retainer-refund liabilities and candidate fee rebates are remitted via the same MT103/LVTS rails with memo codes identifying the reversal and the original invoice.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts (plain-vanilla FX forwards) with a Schedule I bank under a standard ISDA Master Agreement or a bilateral bank forward confirm; maturities aligned to the LP's retainer-projection cycle (30, 60, or 90 days).
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR) for hedging recurring multi-quarter retainer flows above CAD 500,000 notional, executed with a Schedule I bank under ISDA/CSA collateral arrangements.
Over-the-counter CAD/USD plain-vanilla options (call and put) for selective hedging where the LP has a contingent placement pipeline but uncertain closing timing; premium paid in cash, no leverage.

Exchange-traded CAD/USD futures and options listed on the Montreal Exchange (TMX Group), subject to the LP's brokerage mandate and regulated derivatives documentation, providing transparent margin-based hedging without ISDA.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally unnecessary and permissible only where a counterparty bank demonstrably cannot settle CAD deliverable; in practice, because CAD is fully convertible, NDFs are disfavored and may trigger enhanced internal-hedging-policy review; if used, they must be executed through a Canadian-authorized derivatives dealer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec annual update declaration (déclaration de mise à jour annuelle), including confirmation of registered office and corporate general partner details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of the date of registration in the Quebec enterprise register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 50 (approx. USD 37) per missing annual update; failure to file for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off by the Registraire des entreprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (including all required schedules and financial statements summaries)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than five months after the partnership's fiscal period end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per partner per month for each completed month of delay, up to a maximum of 12 months; additional penalties apply for wilfully false statements or omissions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is mandated for a Quebec limited partnership (LP) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises or the Quebec Civil Code. An audit may become contractually required by lenders, investors, or the partnership agreement, or may be requested by the tax authorities during a compliance review.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP; IFRS is required for publicly accountable enterprises, but a private limited partnership may use Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); taxable income is then adjusted under the Income Tax Act and the Taxation Act (Quebec).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec has no standalone annual UBO filing requirement for a limited partnership. The annual update declaration to REQ confirms the general partner's identity and address and, if the general partner is a legal person, the names and addresses of its directors. Any transfer of partnership interests must be recorded in the partnership's register and reflected in an immediate declaration amendment if it changes the public data; otherwise, the next annual update captures the transfer.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (recording partnership interest transfers and beneficial ownership)
Register of Directors of the Corporate General Partner (if applicable)
Minute Book (partnership resolutions, general partner consents, and annual documentation)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Federal 15% + Quebec 11.5% = combined 26.5% (general corporate rate, non-resident-owned corporations may be subject only to federal rate under Part XIV).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction reduces combined federal+Quebec rate to approximately 12.2% on first $500,000 of active business income; Quebec and federal SR&ED credits, patent box-type incentives, and refundable film/local tax credits may apply; a Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent and does not itself pay corporate income tax — partners are taxed on their allocated share.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T5013 Partnership Information Return (federal CRA) — filed electronically via CRA My Business Account or a CRA-approved E-file service.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: If the partnership fiscal period ends on December 31, the return must be filed no later than March 31 of the immediately following year; if the fiscal period ends on any other date, the return is due within five months after the end of that fiscal period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, partnership business number (BN), registered office address, fiscal period start date and end date, legal type (limited partnership), and business activity code (NAICS 561312).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full registered address outside Canada; include country code and, if the non-resident partner is a filing employee, enter the partner's non-resident permanent establishment data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name, address, account reference (SIN or BN), jurisdiction of residence, percentage share of income/loss, and limited or general partner classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner, enter the home/residence address, country code, and the partner's Canadian BN (for corporations) or continuously available SIN for individuals; do not use a mail forwarding address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Statement of income and expenses (T5013, Box 1a)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from executive search and headhunting fees (retainers, success fees), operating expenses, interest expense, and any deductible amounts for salaries, contract labour, business development, rent, and professional services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source income attributable to the LP's permanent establishment; non-resident partners' shares are subject to Part XIII withholding unless covered by treaty exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Allocation of net income/loss (Box 1b, Schedule 1 Part B)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation to each partner of the partnership's net accounting income, taxable income, capital gains, and losses per the partnership agreement and applicable tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident partners, show the allocated amount in the partner's Canadian-source active business income and capital gains; attach supporting calculations and indicate treaty article relied upon.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of any foreign-source income included in the partner's share, foreign taxes deemed payable, and source-country attribution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners generally exclude foreign-source income that is not attributable to the Canadian PE; provide full cross-border jurisdictional breakdown.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information regarding the LP's connected branch operations, cross-border transactions, or solicitation activity with non-resident customers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a complete description of Canadian activities carried on for or with non-residents to support any PE exemption claim.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of $25 per day per partner, minimum $100 and maximum $2,500 per partner; a further penalty equal to the greater of $100 and $25 per day (max $2,500) for each member where the return is more than 24 months outstanding; gross negligence penalties under s. 163(2) may reach 50% of tax evaded; criminal liability for willful evasion may include fines and imprisonment up to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Revenu Québec Relevé 15 (RL-15), plus Québec Partnership Return (CO-17) — filed electronically via Revenu Québec's 'clic Revenu' or authorized online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than March 31 following the partnership's fiscal year-end for calendar-year fiscal periods; for non-calendar year-ends, within five months after the fiscal period end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner legal name, address, date of admission / withdrawal, and quantum of income (profits) or losses credited to the partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the residence status (non-resident) and country code; if the partner is not present in Quebec, still issue an RL-15 if the partner has allocated Quebec-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The amount of the partnership's Quebec-source income or loss allocated to each partner for the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Quebec-only allocation and calculate the proportion of each partner's share attributable to Quebec; non-resident partners must receive a copy for their non-resident Canadian tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocable capital gain or loss to each partner, including from disposition of partnership assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The amounts remain taxable in Quebec if the property is taxable Canadian property; include a note that the partner must file a Quebec return to claim the allocation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file an RL-15 carries a penalty of $25 per day per partner, minimum $100, maximum $2,500; in addition, Revenu Québec may impose a fine of $1,000 to $25,000 for false statements plus 20-40% of the tax sought to be evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) for dividends paid to a non-resident recipient; for a limited partnership, cash distributions of retained income retain their character as partnership income and are not dividends — withholding on the income allocation to a non-resident partner is typically assessed on the allocable amount under Part XIII at 25% or at a reduced treaty rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident partner must file a completed Form NR301 (Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits under a Tax Treaty) with the partnership or directly with CRA, accompanied by an official Certificate of Residence from the partner's home tax authority; the certificate must state the treaty jurisdiction and the relevant treaty article limiting withholding; CRA will validate the claim before the reduced withholding rate is applied.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding rates: royalties 25%; interest 25% (subject to an exemption for arm's-length interest on certain debt obligations). Under the Canada–US tax treaty: interest generally 0%; royalties generally 10% for most intellectual property. Quebec does not impose a separate provincial withholding tax on royalty or interest payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: $1,000,000 CAD (threshold for filing Form T106 – Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents; consolidated group revenue of €750 million triggers Country-by-Country Reporting).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the Gulf style; however, the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) and treaty abuse provisions are applied to disregard transactions lacking genuine economic substance. A limited partnership must demonstrate real office presence, management, business purpose, and sufficient personnel in Quebec to defend its corporate residency and treaty eligibility, especially where the executive search platform generates significant cross-border revenue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly reporting false or exaggerated expenses, understating gross revenues from executive placement retainers, failing to allocate income to a Canadian permanent establishment, or omitting income from non-resident partners in T5013 / RL-15 filings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% of the tax evaded under s. 163(2); criminal conviction under s. 239(1) punishable by a fine of not less than 50% of the tax evaded and up to 5 years imprisonment; CRA may reassess beyond the normal three-year period in cases of misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners of the LP can be held jointly and severally liable for the partnership's unremitted taxes, interest, and penalties under the Income Tax Act s. 227.1 if they directed or allowed the fraudulent filing; travel bans, asset seizures, and personal bankruptcy orders may follow a criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Commercial Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the LP as a nominee or conduit to invoice Canadian executive search services offshore without any meaningful board decisions, physical presence, or operational substance in Quebec, in an attempt to manufacture tax treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA application of GAAR (s. 245) to deny treaty benefits, recharacterize income as taxable in Quebec, impose interest and penalties, and recast transactions at fair market value; potentially a 25% avoidance penalty plus restitution of avoided Canadian tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partners who designed or beneficially controlled the shell arrangement may be personally assessed for the tax shortfall if they exercised dominion or control over the partnership's assets; civil fraud remedies include restitution, injunctions, and detention orders on outbound remittances.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving large retainer or success fees via opaque wire transfers from non-resident clients without performing know-your-client and beneficial-ownership due diligence, or failing to register with FINTRAC and file a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) when payments exceeded the $10,000 CAD cash reporting threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) of up to $100,000 per violation for individuals and $500,000 for entities; repeated or willful non-compliance can result in criminal prosecution with fines up to $1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may be personally penalized if they knowingly failed to implement a compliance regime, authorized a transaction designed to circumvent reporting thresholds, or traded with sanctions-listed persons; a court can issue a travel ban and freeze personal assets pending forfeiture or restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the LP to pay contract headhunter commissions or employee salaries without properly withholding Canadian payroll deductions, or directing amounts to offshore accounts to avoid CRA and Revenu Québec remittances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The CRA may issue a requirement to pay for the unremitted amounts, impose a 10% penalty on the net deficiency, interest at prescribed rates, and assess director liability; criminal sanctions under the Income Tax Act include fines and up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Every person who was a director or general partner of the LP at the time of the failure is jointly and severally liable for the unremitted amounts under s. 227.1, with no due-diligence defence where the non-remittance was intentional; civil judgments may extend to seizure of personal property and restrictions on international travel.
